Iceberg: drop a table (with purge)

import tempfile

import polars as pl
from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog

d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
cat = SqlCatalog("lake", uri=f"sqlite:///{d}/c.db", warehouse=f"file://{d}")
pl.LazyFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": [10, 20]}).sink_iceberg(
    "sales.orders",
    catalog=cat,
    mode="append",
    create_if_not_exists=True,
    create_namespace_if_not_exists=True,
)
tbl = cat.load_table("sales.orders")
cat.drop_table("sales.orders")   # or cat.purge_table(...) to delete the files too

Iceberg: update rows by predicate

import tempfile

import polars as pl
from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog

d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
cat = SqlCatalog("lake", uri=f"sqlite:///{d}/c.db", warehouse=f"file://{d}")
pl.LazyFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": [10, 20]}).sink_iceberg(
    "sales.orders",
    catalog=cat,
    mode="append",
    create_if_not_exists=True,
    create_namespace_if_not_exists=True,
)
tbl = cat.load_table("sales.orders")
import pyarrow as pa

# pyiceberg has no UPDATE either: read the matching rows, change them,
# and overwrite them with a filter
rows = pl.scan_iceberg(tbl).filter(pl.col("id") == 1).with_columns(v=pl.lit(0))
tbl.overwrite(rows.collect().to_arrow(), overwrite_filter="id = 1")

scan_iceberg: answer min/max from the manifest statistics without reading the data files

import os

import tempfile

import polars as pl
from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog

d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
cat = SqlCatalog("lake", uri=f"sqlite:///{d}/c.db", warehouse=f"file://{d}")
pl.LazyFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": [10, 20]}).sink_iceberg(
    "sales.orders",
    catalog=cat,
    mode="append",
    create_if_not_exists=True,
    create_namespace_if_not_exists=True,
)
tbl = cat.load_table("sales.orders")

# delete the data files, to show which queries read them
for p in tbl.inspect.files()["file_path"].to_pylist():
    os.remove(p.removeprefix("file://"))

print(pl.scan_iceberg(tbl).select(pl.len()).collect())
print(pl.scan_iceberg(tbl).select(pl.col("id").max()).collect())
